# Dimension mapping

[CogPO](http://www.cogpo.org/) describes an experimental condition along three
dimensions with closed vocabularies: the stimulus (its modality, kind and role), the
response (the body part and the kind of overt act) and the instructions. This page maps
every value of those six vocabularies to the [HED schema](https://www.hedtags.org/) tag
that expresses it, in HED 8.4.0, and records where HED has no such tag. It is the
value-level companion of [HED vs CogPO](hed_vs_cogpo.md), as the [task mapping](task_mapping.md)
page is of [The Catalog vs CogPO](the_catalog_vs_cogpo.md).

The source of record is `data/facet_defs.tsv`, which also holds the values the Catalog
would add if it adopts these vocabularies as facets; see the section on facets below.

## What a facet would be

A **facet** is a single attribute of a task, taken from a closed vocabulary, that a
repository could filter on: stimulus modality is one facet, with values such as
`visual` and `auditory`; response kind is another, with `button_press` and `saccade`. A
task would carry one or more values on each facet, chosen for its canonical procedure.
The idea is that a task name says what the participant was asked to do as a whole,
while its facets say what was shown, done and instructed, the same three things CogPO
describes for a condition, and the same things HED tags on the events.

CogPO's six dimensions are the natural first six facets, which is why their values are
kept here with a HED tag each. Whether the Catalog adopts facets, in this form or another,
and how they relate to CogPO's paradigm classes and to the pseudo tasks, is not settled.
No task record carries facet values, and nothing on the site depends on them; this page
stands on its own as a CogPO-to-HED mapping.

## How the table was built

Each CogPO value was kept with its CogPO definition and identifier, and given the HED
8.4.0 tag or tags that express it. Where HED has the same concept under the same or an
equivalent name the note says "Exact tag"; where it has only a parent or a neighbour the
note names it; where it has nothing the tag column is empty and the note says why.

Two kinds of value were added, against the day the vocabularies become facets. **From
HED**: roles and instructions that HED has, CogPO lacks and the Catalog's tasks would
need, such as the distractor, cue, oddball, stop-signal and prime roles and the judge,
recognize, predict, plan and switch-attention instructions. **By the Catalog**: values
neither resource has, such as monetary amounts and playing cards as stimuli, rating as a
response, and choose, withhold and navigate as instructions. Every row's `source` column
says which, so the CogPO-to-HED mapping can be read on its own by ignoring the rest.

Nothing was dropped from CogPO's vocabularies. The values that are out of the Catalog's
scope, acupuncture, TMS, infusion, micturition, stay in the tables so that the
correspondence is complete.

## Stimulus modality

CogPO's six modalities map one to one onto HED's `Sensory-presentation` tags, and its
four tactile subtypes onto a presentation tag plus a `Tactile-attribute` or
`Somatic-attribute`. The one gap is interoception, which HED 8.4.0 does not name.

```{include} ../_generated/cogpo_dimension_stimulus_modality.md
```

## Stimulus kind

CogPO's 41 explicit stimuli are the widest vocabulary and the one where HED's coverage
is most uneven. Language items (`Word`, `Pseudoword`, `Syllable`, `Character`), sounds
(`Tone`, `Click`, `Signal-noise`, `Musical-sound`, `Vocalized-sound`), faces, images and
geometric objects (`Dots`, `Pattern`, `2D-shape`) are all present. HED has no item for
a digit or a number, for food, an odor or a puff of air, for speech as a stimulus, or
for the physiological stimuli (electrical, thermal, laser, infusion, TMS). Note also that
HED's `Letter` is a piece of correspondence, so an alphabetic letter is a `Character`.

```{include} ../_generated/cogpo_dimension_stimulus_kind.md
```

## Stimulus role

CogPO's four roles exist only on its wiki; the OWL class has no members. All four are
HED tags. HED's `Task-stimulus-role` vocabulary is much richer, and eight more of its
values are listed as Catalog candidates.

```{include} ../_generated/cogpo_dimension_stimulus_role.md
```

## Response modality

CogPO's body parts are Foundational Model of Anatomy classes with no label in the OWL;
the labels here were checked against the FMA through the EBI Ontology Lookup Service.
HED's `Body-part` subtree has every one except arm and leg, for which the parent
`Upper-extremity` or `Lower-extremity` stands in.

```{include} ../_generated/cogpo_dimension_response_modality.md
```

## Response kind

HED's `Action` subtree covers the common responses directly (`Press`, `Saccade`,
`Blink`, `Speak`, `Point`, `Grasp`, `Write`, `Swallow`, `Hold-breath`, `Smile`,
`Whistle`). A button press is two tags, the action `Press` and the device pressed
(`Push-button`, `Keyboard-key` or `Mouse-button`), which is why three device-specific
values are listed beside CogPO's single Button Press. HED has no tap, draw or
drink action, and a rating is a `Participant-response` carrying a value rather than an
action of its own.

```{include} ../_generated/cogpo_dimension_response_kind.md
```

## Instructions

CogPO's instruction verbs are almost all HED `Think` or `Perform` actions
(`Attend-to`, `Count`, `Detect`, `Discriminate`, `Encode`, `Generate`, `Imagine`,
`Recall`, `Track`, `Read`, `Repeat`, `Rest`). Name is the exception: HED has `Identify`
for the judgement and `Speak` for the response but no naming action. HED's `Think`
vocabulary is larger than CogPO's and supplies eight instructions the Catalog's tasks
would need; five more (choose, rate, withhold, navigate, play) are Catalog candidates,
and only play has a HED tag.

```{include} ../_generated/cogpo_dimension_instructions.md
```

## What the tables do not settle

Whether the Catalog adopts these vocabularies as facets at all, and if so whether a task
record stores the plain value (`words`, `button_press`) or the HED tag. The tables keep
both so that either choice can be made later without redoing the work. The HED schema
version is 8.4.0 throughout, and a schema release that adds a missing item or action
changes the tag column, not CogPO's values.
